plan.planning_summary: Building on iteration_01 route_01 (24-layer HfO2/SiO2 periodic stack, best_target_score=0.5346, valid_candidates=9), this round addresses the low valid candidate count by restructuring thickness initialization. Feedback indicates the 200 nm uniform baseline caused boundary collisions; new routes initialize near quarter-wave optical thickness (100-135 nm for HfO2/SiO2 at band centers) with bounded perturbations. Three complementary routes explore: (1) improved 24-layer initialization with gradient optimizer, (2) reduced 20-layer stack for manufacturability, (3) increased 28-layer stack for performance ceiling. All routes preserve the dual-band objective (high transmission 1000-1700 nm, high reflection 300-450 nm) and 30-layer maximum constraint.

routes.title: Quarter-Wave Initialized 24-Layer Stack with Gradient Optimization
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses near quarter-wave optical thickness (HfO2 ~100-110 nm, SiO2 ~125-135 nm at 450 nm center) rather than uniform 200 nm will reduce boundary collisions during optimization, increasing valid_candidates while maintaining or improving best_target_score above 0.53.
routes.design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory predicts maximum reflectance for minimum layer count when optical thickness equals lambda/4. For dual-band operation (UV reflection, SWIR transmission), non-quarter-wave deviations are necessary but quarter-wave initialization provides a physically meaningful starting point closer to optimal solutions.

design_variables: thickness bounds 80-200 nm for HfO2, 100-180 nm for SiO2
manufacturing_considerations: outermost SiO2 layer >= 100 nm for durability
thickness bounds reflect realistic deposition control
theory_basis: Dual-band filter requires non-quarter-wave optimization from quarter-wave seed
expected_advantages: Higher valid_candidates due to reduced boundary collisions
Faster convergence from physically meaningful initialization
known_risks: Quarter-wave initialization may trap optimizer in local optimum
Dual-band conflict may still limit best_target_score below 0.7
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate. Stack sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica (12 bilayers, 24 finite layers total). Initialize HfO2 layers at 105 nm and SiO2 layers at 130 nm (quarter-wave at 450 nm center). Apply gradient-based thickness optimization with bounds: HfO2 80-200 nm, SiO2 100-180 nm. Evaluate coherent TMM at normal incidence across 300-450 nm (reflectance target) and 1000-1700 nm (transmittance target). Maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band and mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band simultaneously. Outermost layer must be SiO2. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
routes.revision_reason: Restructured thickness initialization from uniform 200 nm to quarter-wave values (HfO2 105 nm, SiO2 130 nm) based on feedback directive to reduce boundary collisions. Maintains 24-layer topology from route_01 but changes seed distribution to concentrate near hypothesized resonance window.

routes.title: Reduced 20-Layer Stack for Manufacturability Trade-off
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Reducing layer count from 24 to 20 will decrease fabrication complexity and stress accumulation while maintaining acceptable dual-band performance, with best_target_score remaining above 0.45.
routes.design_principle: Fewer layers reduce deposition time, stress accumulation, and interface defects. Evidence shows 38-layer designs present fabrication challenges; staying well below 30-layer limit provides margin. Quarter-wave theory predicts reflectance scales with layer count, so 20 layers may suffice for moderate UV reflection while preserving SWIR transmission.

routes.title: Extended 28-Layer Stack for Performance Ceiling Exploration
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 24 to 28 (still within 30-layer limit) will improve UV reflectance through increased stopband strength while maintaining SWIR transmission, achieving best_target_score above 0.60.
routes.design_principle: Higher bilayer count increases stopband reflectance for quarter-wave stacks. Evidence shows 38-layer designs achieve >99.9% reflectance at multiple wavelengths. Using 28 layers (14 bilayers) stays within 30-layer constraint while maximizing reflectance potential for UV suppression band.

research_influence: Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:225461372 supports using needle optimization and non-quarter-wave designs for multi-wavelength HR coatings, motivating the gradient optimizer choice in route_02.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:4902694 provides quarter-wave stack theory foundation for initialization values (lambda/4 optical thickness) used in all three routes.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:270229843 demonstrates 79-layer HfO2/SiO2 stacks for high-reflection applications, supporting the feasibility of high-layer-count designs within route_04.
Evidence s2-chunk:CorpusId:283155301 shows 4-layer AR optimization with bounded thickness, supporting the bounded optimization strategy across all routes.
unresolved_decisions: Angle of incidence not specified in original request - all routes assume normal incidence for initial design; oblique incidence performance requires separate verification.
Polarization state not specified - all routes assume unpolarized or normal incidence where polarization effects are minimal.
Environmental durability requirements beyond outermost SiO2 layer not quantified - routes include >= 100 nm SiO2 outermost layer based on evidence but specific thickness threshold is assumption.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
